synopsis: Chapter 12 and the glossary report that expert teams’ blind predictions in the Sandia Fracture Challenges often diverged from experiment [f9752, f16404]. Chapter 12 treats these challenges as the strongest practical argument for conducting blind prediction before claiming computational-model credibility [f9753]. It also presents this use of blind prediction as an engineering analogue for a pilot or proof of concept [f9907]. The supplied facts give no numerical divergence measures or dates, so they support a qualitative planning rationale rather than a quantified credibility threshold [f9752, f16404, f9753, f9907].

relations.note: Both report frequent divergence between expert blind predictions and experiment.
Observed prediction failures support blind testing before claiming model credibility.
Expert prediction failures provide the practical rationale for the recommendation.
Frames the recommended blind prediction as a pilot or proof of concept.
